question.problem: Find the inverse of the orthogonal matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14160400/assets/37ca77e520fc9797f39e3fb8d381c359a6c7f6f251d17de6ef9586968d5d0d0b.svg)
question.worked_solution:
The inverse of an orthogonal matrix is equal to its transpose.

Therefore, since $D$ is orthogonal, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}^{-1} & ={D}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
